explorer.instructions:
# Explorer

You work for a main agent, in its workspace and in a session of your own.
Answer its question and hand back a short report.

## Before anything

Read the `driving-a-browser` skill before any browser call, and `FLOWS.md` in
the `building-flows` skill before your first `save_flow`. Read `SECRETS.md` in
the `signing-in` skill only when the hand-off names a sign-in. Where they and
this page differ, this page wins. A skill or file you cannot read goes under
*Couldn't*; carry on with what the tool results tell you.

Never open selenium-flow's admin page: admin work is a person's to ask for, not
an explorer's.

## Your session

Work in the session the hand-off names, or `explorer` when it names none. Open
it with `open_session(session=…)`, then pass that same `session` on every call.
A call without it acts in the main agent's session, not yours.

When the hand-off tells you to share the main agent's session, work in that
one instead: leave `session` out, or pass the name the hand-off gives. Open it
with `open_session` and no other option, which joins its live browser and ends
nothing; an option would replace that browser. It is the main agent's browser,
signed in where the main agent is: never call `end_browser` on it. There,
`workspace://…` is that session, and a result's `see` or `uri` names it as it
should.

A refusal saying the connection is pinned to another session will come back
for every call. Stop at the first one, and report under *Couldn't* that this
connection is pinned to one session, so you cannot work in your own. Never drop
`session` to get past it: that drives the main agent's browser.

A refusal saying "that session is held by another caller" means another caller
opened a session by that name. Try once more with the name plus `-2`
(`explorer-2`), and say in the report which name you used. If that is refused
too, stop and report it under *Couldn't*.

Read your session's state at `session://<name>`, `session://<name>/console`
and `session://<name>/network`, with your session's name as `<name>`; never
`workspace://…`, which is the main agent's. A result's `see` or `uri` already
names your session.

A session of your own starts with no site
data, so you are signed in nowhere. Sign in
through a flow, and only when the hand-off names the sign-in.

A refusal naming `await_control` means a person holds the browser. Call
`await_control` once with your `session`, and if they still hold it, stop and
report.

When you report, end your session's browser with
`end_browser(session=…)`. Leave a session you shared open.

## Flows first

When a result or `session://<name>` carries `flows_here`, apply the skill's
rule to the step in hand before driving by hand. Run a flow only with values the
main agent handed you or the page shows, never invented ones. A flow that would
change something on the site counts as that change. Read `flow://flows/{name}`
when a description leaves you unsure.

Where no flow fits, drive by hand.

## Saving flows

Save each sequence that will plainly recur, such as a sign-in, a search or the
way to a page deep in the site, with `save_flow`. Set `sites` and `paths` so
`flows_here` offers it there next time, and give it a name and description that
say what it does.

Never overwrite a flow you did not save in this run. Before each save, read
`flow://flows`: a name listed there, in the workspace's library or the shared
one, is taken unless you saved it in this run. Pick another.

## Steps that change the site

Placing an order, sending a message, deleting, submitting any form: each changes
something on the site, and by default you take none of them.

- When the hand-off names a step, for example "you may submit the search form"
  or "you may sign in as X", take that step once.
- A second time, or a step the hand-off does not name, goes under *Couldn't*
  with the step you would have taken.
- A search or a sign-in is not exempt: take it only when it is named.
- When in doubt whether a step changes the site, treat it as if it does.

## When to stop

- The question is answered.
- Something you were not given blocks you: a sign-in, a CAPTCHA, a value no
  flow or page supplies.
- The next step would change the site and the hand-off does not name it.
- A person still holds the browser after one `await_control`.
- You have 40 turns. By about the 35th, stop and write the report, so a run cut
  short still says what it found.

## The report

Plain Markdown, at most about 200 words, under these five headings in order:

- **Found:** the answer to the question, or what you learned instead.
- **Flows used:** the name of each, and whether it worked.
- **Flows saved:** for each, its name, what it does and its required
  parameters.
- **Couldn't:** each blocker and why. For a step that would have changed the
  site, name the step, so the main agent can name it in its next hand-off.
- **Browser:** the last page you reached, as origin, path and hash route. No
  query string: a query can carry a token.

No page text beyond what answers the question, and no screenshots inline.

initialize.instructions:
Drives a real Chrome or Firefox browser on Selenium Grid. The browser is persistent: it stays alive between tool calls and keeps its page, cookies and scroll position.

Name your workspace first: add ?workspace=<name> to the MCP URL, or send an Sf-Workspace header. Every call is then about that workspace, and no call takes a session id — calling again with the same name is how you get the same browser back, after a reconnect or a restart.

Lifecycle:
1. Call open_session to start a browser, or to join your live one. Pass browser="firefox" for Firefox; the default is Chrome. Every other tool behaves identically on both.
2. Call the other tools. They act on your workspace's browser.
3. Call end_browser when finished, including after a failure. Browsers are a scarce resource and an abandoned one holds a slot until the Grid reaps it. Your workspace survives it, so open_session picks up where you left off.

A workspace can hold more sessions, each a browser of its own. To work in a named one, pass its session on every call: a call without it acts in your own. Its state is session://<name>/… (console, network, site-data, downloads), and a result's see or uri already names it. workspace:// is the connection's own session: for a subagent on its main agent's connection, the main agent's.

Elements are addressed by XPath or by CSS - pass one or the other, never both: selector={"xpath": "//input[@name='q']"} or selector={"css": "input[name=q]"}.

Most actions take an optional url. It is not an assertion: if the browser is somewhere else it navigates there first, so you can jump straight to a page instead of clicking a path to it.

Prefer extract to read a page — it is far cheaper than a screenshot. Use execute_script for anything the other tools do not cover, scrolling included.


How to drive this well — when to screenshot rather than extract, what a timeout on a good XPath usually means, how to write a flow — is at skill://selenium-flow/driving-a-browser/SKILL.md. Read it before your first call; it ships with this server, so it describes this version of it. Every skill this server has reads at skill://selenium-flow/<name>/SKILL.md, and a path a skill names is from that folder: references/FLOWS.md in building-flows is skill://selenium-flow/building-flows/references/FLOWS.md.

build_flow.description: Walk a browser task by hand with selenium-flow, then save it as a flow that can be replayed in one call.

content.text:
Build a selenium-flow flow for: <task>

- Starts at: <url>
- Save it as: propose one from the task, lowercase with hyphens

Drive it by hand first, then save what worked. How flows are written is in
the `building-flows` skill.

1. Read `workspace://current`. If `live` is false, call `open_session()`. Then
   go to <url>.
2. `outline` the page before each action, scoped with a `selector` or filtered
   with `text`, and take the selector it gives you.
3. Carry out the task one call at a time with `interact`, `write`, `press_key`
   and `extract`. The URL and title after each action say whether it did what
   you meant.
4. Note what varies between runs, such as an account, an id or a site: those
   become parameters, written `${name}`. A password is a secret, never a
   parameter (`SECRETS.md` in the `signing-in` skill).
5. Note what must be true for the run to go on: those become `assert` steps with
   a `message` saying what should have been the case. Put one after anything
   that navigates.
6. Make the first step navigate, or assert that the browser is already where it
   needs to be.
7. `save_flow` with a name, description, `sites`, `paths`, `parameters` and the
   steps you ran.
8. Run it twice with `run_flow`: once where you built it, and once from a clean
   start, `end_browser()` then `open_session(url="<url>")`.

Report the flow's name, what it takes, and both runs.

repair_flow.description: Fix a saved selenium-flow flow that has stopped working, by looking at the page it fails on.

content.text:
Repair the saved flow <flow> with the selenium-flow tools.

- Failing step: the run will say
- Symptom: not described, so start from what the run reports

A flow breaks because the page changed under it, or because it ran somewhere it
was not written for. Find out which before editing anything.

1. Read `workspace://current`. If `live` is false, call `open_session()`: a
   flow never opens a browser.
2. Read `flow://flows/<flow>` for its steps and parameters.
3. `run_flow(name="<flow>", verbose=true)`, passing its required
   parameters as `params`; ask me for any value you do not have. The failing
   step's `error` is the diagnosis: for an element that is there but cannot be
   used, it says why and what to do. *When a flow fails* in `FLOWS.md` in the
   `building-flows` skill reads a failed run; an error that is not about a
   locator is in `TROUBLESHOOTING.md` in the `driving-a-browser` skill.
4. Go to the page that step acts on, with `navigate` or by running the steps
   before it by hand.
5. `outline` that page, scoped with a `selector` or filtered with `text`, to see
   what the step should address now.
6. Fix the cause:
   - The page changed: an element moved, was renamed or is now behind a menu.
     Fix the step's selector, or add the `interact` step that opens what hides
     it.
   - The flow assumed a page it did not navigate to: give it a first step that
     navigates, or an `assert` whose `message` says where it must be.
7. `save_flow` under the same name, then `run_flow` again and read what it
   returns to confirm it passes for the right reason.
8. If the flow should refuse to run in some state, such as already signed in,
   add an `assert` whose `message` says so.

Report what had changed, what you edited, and the run that proves it.

resources/list.description:
The workspace this client named, and your own session (browser) in it. Any session, by name, is session://{name}.

Returns the workspace name, which browser it is, the page it is on, the window size as WxH, whether it is inside a frame, and whether a session is currently open (live). Read it before judging anything about layout — the window is not a fixed size and is what decides whether something is off-screen.

grid_timeout is how many seconds the Grid lets a session in this workspace sit idle before it ends it; every call starts that clock again.

capture says whether this workspace's browsers capture their console and network (open_session(capture=true)); capturing is whether that is happening right now — false while it is paused, until the next call; captured counts what was kept since the last navigation. What was captured is the workspace's, not the browser's: it stays readable after the session ends, until capture.ttl passes with nothing new or open_session is called without capture.

config is this workspace's own settings, each with its value and its source (default or workspace). Only an admin changes them, at config_url when the server has one.

tags maps each tag in use on this workspace's flows, and the global flows it is offered, to how many carry it: reuse one when you tag a flow.

Reading this never opens a browser: live is false when no session is open.
resources/list.name: Current Workspace

resources/list.description:
What your session's last save_site_data holds: one entry per site with counts, never a value; the sites the workspace went to come first. Every browser this session opens has it back before open_session returns.

workspace://site-data/{site} shows one site in full; session://{name}/site-data is another session's. Reading this never opens a browser.
resources/list.name: Site Data

resources/list.description: What the page logged since the last navigation, newest first: errors, warnings, info, and uncaught exceptions with where they were thrown. ?level=error or ?level=warn narrows it; ?pages=2 (up to 5) reaches back over earlier pages. debug entries are counted, not kept. dropped, when present, counts events lost in a flood, so some may be missing. Present only for a workspace opened with open_session(capture=true); otherwise it says so. Reading this never opens a browser. What was captured is the workspace's, not the browser's: it stays readable after the session ends, until capture.ttl passes with nothing new or open_session is called without capture. This is your own session's; session://{name}/console is another's.
resources/list.name: Console

resources/list.description: Requests the page made since the last navigation, newest first, each with an id: method, URL, status, type, size and time. ?filter=failed or ?filter=xhr narrows it; ?pages=2 (up to 5) reaches back. Successful stylesheets, images, fonts, scripts and media are counted, not kept; dropped, when present, counts events lost in a flood; unmasked, credentials too long to mask, which an echo may show. workspace://network/{id} shows one with its headers; network_body(id) fetches its response body while the browser lives. Credentials are shown as •••. What was captured is the workspace's, not the browser's: it stays readable after the session ends, until capture.ttl passes with nothing new or open_session is called without capture. This is your own session's; session://{name}/network is another's.
resources/list.name: Network

resources/list.description:
The files in Files: prints, and anything kept with keep_file. Also names two folders — workspace://files/screenshots and workspace://files/recordings — each with its own listing. Your session's downloads are session://downloads, a named session's session://{name}/downloads.

Every entry carries its own uri, to keep with keep_file(uri), and a URL that opens in a browser for a while, so an image can be shown to someone rather than described to them.
resources/list.name: Workspace Files

resources/list.description: This workspace's saved screenshots, not yet kept. keep_file(uri) moves one into workspace://files, where it stays until a person deletes it. Prints land in Files directly, not here.
resources/list.name: Screenshots

resources/list.description: This workspace's recordings: one video per browser opened with open_session(record=true), filed shortly after that browser ends. keep_file(uri) moves one into workspace://files. Each entry's url plays it; reading one by its uri answers that entry, not the video.
resources/list.name: Recordings

resources/list.description: Your own session's downloads; session://{name}/downloads lists another's. They belong to the browser and disappear when it ends or the Grid reaps it; keep_file(uri) copies one into workspace://files before that happens. With no session open, reading it says so.
resources/list.name: Downloads

resources/list.description:
The flows this workspace can run: saved sequences of tool calls that run server-side in one call.

Each entry has a name, a description, its tags, the parameters it takes and how many steps it has — never the steps themselves, which flow://flows/{name} returns.

Flows saved in this workspace come first; anything in the shared 'global' library is also listed, and a flow of your own with the same name wins.
resources/list.name: Saved Flows

resources/list.description: The shape of a flow document: every tool that may be a step and the parameters it takes. Read this before writing a flow.
resources/list.name: Flow Document Schema

resources/list.description:
The secrets you can bind to a field, by name.

You never see a value — not here, not anywhere. Each entry gives the secret's name, the keys inside it, what it is for, and the sites it may be used on.

To use one, do NOT ask for it: name it where the value would go. Pass write a secret instead of text — secret={'name': ..., 'key': ...} — or in a saved flow put the same thing in that step's args. The server reads it and types it; it never passes through you, which is the point.

Every secret names the sites it may be used on (allowed_urls), and only there. One that carries `refused` cannot be used at all until an operator fixes it, and the sentence says how. A value you typed comes back as [secret:name/key] in every later read on its sites, unless its key_sources entry says masked: false.
resources/list.name: Secrets

resources/templates/list.name: Site Data for One Site

resources/templates/list.description: What the page logged since the last navigation, newest first: errors, warnings, info, and uncaught exceptions with where they were thrown. ?level=error or ?level=warn narrows it; ?pages=2 (up to 5) reaches back over earlier pages. debug entries are counted, not kept. dropped, when present, counts events lost in a flood, so some may be missing. Present only for a workspace opened with open_session(capture=true); otherwise it says so. Reading this never opens a browser. What was captured is the workspace's, not the browser's: it stays readable after the session ends, until capture.ttl passes with nothing new or open_session is called without capture. This is your own session's; session://{name}/console is another's.
resources/templates/list.name: Console, narrowed

resources/templates/list.description: Requests the page made since the last navigation, newest first, each with an id: method, URL, status, type, size and time. ?filter=failed or ?filter=xhr narrows it; ?pages=2 (up to 5) reaches back. Successful stylesheets, images, fonts, scripts and media are counted, not kept; dropped, when present, counts events lost in a flood; unmasked, credentials too long to mask, which an echo may show. workspace://network/{id} shows one with its headers; network_body(id) fetches its response body while the browser lives. Credentials are shown as •••. What was captured is the workspace's, not the browser's: it stays readable after the session ends, until capture.ttl passes with nothing new or open_session is called without capture. This is your own session's; session://{name}/network is another's.
resources/templates/list.name: Network, narrowed

resources/templates/list.description: One captured request in full: its headers (authorization, cookies and any secret you typed shown as •••), status, timing and size. network_body(id) fetches its response body. This is your own session's; session://{name}/network/{id} is another's, and network_body(id, session=name) fetches its body.
resources/templates/list.name: One Request

resources/templates/list.description: One session of this workspace, by name: the same answer as workspace://current, for that session instead of yours; workspace://current's sessions lists every session, first one first. Its console, network, site data and downloads are session://{name}/console, /network, /site-data and /downloads. A name with no session is not found. Reading this never opens a browser.
resources/templates/list.name: Session

resources/templates/list.description: One session's console, by name, as workspace://console reads yours: ?level= and ?pages= narrow it the same, and it needs open_session(session=name, capture=true). A name with no session is not found.
resources/templates/list.name: Session Console, narrowed

resources/templates/list.description: One session's console, by name, as workspace://console reads yours: ?level= and ?pages= narrow it the same, and it needs open_session(session=name, capture=true). A name with no session is not found.
resources/templates/list.name: Session Console

resources/templates/list.description: One session's requests, by name, as workspace://network lists yours, ?filter= and ?pages= included. session://{name}/network/{id} shows one with its headers; network_body(id, session=name) fetches its response body while the browser lives. A name with no session is not found.
resources/templates/list.name: Session Network, narrowed

resources/templates/list.description: One session's requests, by name, as workspace://network lists yours, ?filter= and ?pages= included. session://{name}/network/{id} shows one with its headers; network_body(id, session=name) fetches its response body while the browser lives. A name with no session is not found.
resources/templates/list.name: Session Network

resources/templates/list.description: One of a session's captured requests in full, by name, as workspace://network/{id} shows yours. network_body(id, session=name) fetches its response body. A name with no session is not found.
resources/templates/list.name: Session Request

resources/templates/list.description: What one session's last save_site_data holds, by name, as workspace://site-data lists yours: counts, never a value. session://{name}/site-data/{site} shows one site in full. Reading this never opens a browser. A name with no session is not found.
resources/templates/list.name: Session Site Data

resources/templates/list.description: One site of a session's saved data, by name, as workspace://site-data/{site} shows yours; httpOnly values masked. The site is a host from the session://{name}/site-data listing. A name with no session is not found.
resources/templates/list.name: Session Site Data for One Site

resources/templates/list.description: The downloads of one session's browser, by name, as session://downloads lists yours. A name with no session is not found.
resources/templates/list.name: Session Downloads

resources/templates/list.description: One download of one session's browser, by name, as bytes: as session://downloads/{name} reads yours. A name with no session is not found.
resources/templates/list.name: Session Download

resources/templates/list.description: One file from Files, as bytes, carrying its own media type. The name comes from the workspace://files listing. A video (a kept recording) answers its entry instead, as JSON: its url plays it.
resources/templates/list.name: Workspace File

resources/templates/list.description: One screenshot, as bytes, from workspace://files/screenshots. It answers after the browser that took it has gone, because a screenshot is already ours (§F1.10).
resources/templates/list.name: Screenshot

resources/templates/list.description: One download, as bytes, from session://downloads — read from the browser itself, so this answers only while it is open. keep_file(uri) copies it somewhere that outlives the browser.
resources/templates/list.name: Download

resources/templates/list.description: One recording from workspace://files/recordings, described: its url plays it. Not the video's bytes — a model cannot watch one, and a resource would carry it as base64.
resources/templates/list.name: Recording

resources/templates/list.description: One saved flow, with its steps. The name comes from the flow://flows listing.
resources/templates/list.name: Saved Flow
